text:
B: Hello! Hello, can you see me?
A: Yeah.
B: Oh good. I'm Agnieszka. It's a hard one, people say "Agnes" sometimes, it's fine.
A: Courtney.
B: Nice to meet you, Courtney. Where are you calling from?
A: Sunderland.
B: Oh, far up! I'm in Yeovil, in Somerset. Very different, I think.
A: Probably, yeah.
B: [laughs] Okay. Erm, did you do the puzzle bit at the start? I was terrible. I think I was too slow.
A: It was all right. I didn't finish the last one.
B: Me also not! Okay, good, so not just me. I'm a care assistant, senior care assistant in a care home, so I'm used to people who can't find their glasses, not puzzles. Sorry, I talk too much, yeah? What do you do?
A: Erm, admin. Lettings office. Phones and that.
B: Do you like it?
A: No. It's fine. It pays for stuff.
B: [laughs] Honest, I like it.
A: Yeah.
B: In your photo, I saw the drawings on the wall behind you. Are they yours?
A: Erm... yeah. Most of them.
B: They looked very detailed, even small on the screen. What do you draw?
A: It's kind of ink stuff, like, fineliner. Hands a lot. Moths. Faces that sort of turn into plants, like the skin goes into leaves and roots. People say it's creepy but I don't think it is, it's more like, things changing into other things. I've been doing hands for months because they're dead hard, there's loads going on in them, all the little lines and the knuckles, and if you get one bit wrong the whole thing looks like a glove. I've got this new pen, it's a point oh three, and it's... sorry. I'm going on.
B: No, no, I like it! You know, at work I see a lot of hands. Old hands, very thin skin, all the lines. One lady, she is ninety-four, her hands are like a map. I always think somebody should draw them.
A: That's actually... yeah. Old hands are the best ones to draw. My nana let me draw hers once.
B: Ah, bless her. You're close to your nana?
A: Yeah. She lives two streets away. She's the one who got me drawing, really.
B: That's lovely. My mum is in Poland, I call her maybe four times a week. We make pierogi together on video, she shouts at me I put too much filling.
A: [laughs] Do you?
B: Always! I'm generous. Do you sell your drawings?
A: A few prints. At a zine fair in Newcastle. And I've got an Instagram, it's anonymous.
B: Anonymous, why?
A: Dunno. Easier. If people hate it, they don't know it's me.
B: Hmm. I don't think they would hate it.
A: You haven't seen it.
B: [laughs] True! But I saw the moth on your hoodie, so I trust you.
A: That's not even mine, it's from Primark.
B: Okay, then I trust Primark.
A: [laughs] Fair.
